scope: Read all 50 passages, all overviews, periods, endings and proposed overrides, plus HANDOFF.md and the saved decoded first-snapshot geometry. Independently reopened 14 selected sources for writing, identity, chronology, household interpretation and numerical claims. This is a bounded review, not certification of every source or the live UI.

findings.result: The early Texas geometry warning matches the decoded footprint and Kavanagh's documented early eighteenth-century New Mexico presence. Modern objects and language witness are explicitly later.

Minnesota and later westward migration supported. Contemporary Southern and Northern communities remain distinct. Modern self-name translation is accurately attributed to the community, important because the older OHS author describes its etymology as uncertain.
No invented 1530 fall. Archival report supports refugee movements in 1711 and 1760, while language avoids asserting extinction of every person.

Archaeological category correctly distinguished from a single named nation; imported 1492 to 1500 interval visibly identified as later than the conventional circa 1450 endpoint. Ending correctly preserves living descendants.

sourcesChecked.checked: Mission sentence and supplied English translation exactly match, including the final combining mark; modern context accurately stated.
Tsistsistas spelling and two translations, crop list, Head Start/child care and Master Apprentice programme.
Explicit absence of Calusa written records; no unsupported original-script specimen invented.
Hohokam archaeological terminology, circa 1450 change, written-language absence, first written visitor accounts with Kino in 1694.
Early 1700s New Mexico, family/tipi organization, councils, fluid group membership, 1966 constitution.

Minnesota origins, later westward migration, different farming and hunting groups; disagreement about self-name etymology noted but current card accurately attributes its translation to tribal source.
Crop and gathered-food claims; fourteenth-century Great House and later settlement changes without single asserted cause.
Refugee movements in 1711 and 1760, Cuba settlement, limited surviving documentary tracks.
Watercourt radiocarbon interval 1300 to 1400, fish-storage interpretation, preserved palm-fibre/wood/seeds/scales and fish taxa. Distinction between physical remains and interpretation preserved.

PDF pages 4, 5, 8 and 9: plaster pits, burned daub impressions, related-household interpretation, tasks, grinding tools, rubbish burning/soil capping with tentative smell/pest explanation. Locator page numbering accurate.
106 drawings, fourteen artists, 1864 to 1869 events, post-Summit Springs recovery; pictures distinguished from phonetic language.
Snaketown unfinished horned-lizard shell with resist, fermented saguaro acid hypothesis and most contexts circa 950 to 1150. Draft preserves proposed-liquid status.
Population movement to smaller villages after 1400 and living Akimel O'odham descendants.
Red River War 1874 to 1875 and forced reservation settlement, consistent with continued community rather than disappearance.

budgetCheck.method: Independent whitespace-token recount by distinct URL, including overview, period titles/summaries, passage texts, ending and any supplied override summary.

limits: Did not independently reopen all Smithsonian object catalogues, Biesterfeldt publication, fish reanalysis, shell-tool counts or every military-history source.
Did not rerun geometry decoding; inspected author's saved decoded properties and bounds.
No runtime files edited and no browser, rendering, navigation or deployment checks performed.
